newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eduscho owner puts sale at 200 million marks.
newsitem.headline: Eduscho owner puts sale at 200 million marks.

text.p: The owner of Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, Rolf Schopf, told German radio on Wednesday the company would be sold to Tchibo Holding AG in Hamburg for 200 million marks, pending monopoly authority approval.
Schopf told Radio Bremen this excluded buildings and sites.

He said he did not achieve the best possible sales price but after two years of sharp losses despite top management changes, he saw no alternative to the sale in order to save the more than 5,000 jobs at stake.
Tchibo, whose coffee arm represents the second largest German coffee roaster, used to be Eduscho's fiercest competitor in the tied coffee outlet market shared by the two.
But while Tchibo managed to stay ahead of the game, Eduscho last had a market share of just 11 percent, according to Schopf.
This meant it was in third, fourth, or fifth position, depending on price campaigns at competing firms Melitta and Aldi, Eduscho spokesman Rolf Helmbrecht said earlier.
Traders fear the move could create a powerful customer in the raw materials market which would try to exert downward pressure on buying prices.
The radio report also said local unions feared the move might bring a concentration of supply services to shops, administration and purchasing.
But the two companies have stated they plan to keep the two individual entities separate.
